# INVESTMENT MEMORANDUM

## Section 1: Executive Summary

**Date:** September 6, 2024

**Transaction Overview:** This joinder agreement adds three new borrowing entities (Innovex Downhole Solutions LLC, Innovex International Inc., and TIW Corporation) to an existing credit facility originally established on June 10, 2022. The existing borrowers include Tercel Oilfield Products USA L.L.C., Pride Energy Services LLC, and Top-Co Inc.

**Transaction Structure:** The agreement represents an expansion of the Second Amended and Restated Revolving Credit, Term Loan, Guaranty and Security Agreement, with PNC Bank National Association serving as agent for the lending syndicate. The transaction appears related to a merger involving Dril-Quip, Inc. (renamed to Innovex International Inc.) and includes corporate restructuring activities.

**Purpose:** The financing supports the post-merger capital structure following the Dril-Quip merger transaction, where Innovex merged into DQ Merger Sub LLC (subsequently renamed Innovex Downhole Solutions LLC).

**Company Background:** The borrowing entities operate in the oilfield products and energy services sector, with operations spanning multiple jurisdictions including Texas, Delaware, and Alberta, Canada.

## Section 2: Investment Highlights & Risks

**Key Strengths/Credit Positives:**
• Established credit facility with amendment history dating to 2022, indicating ongoing lender support
• Diversified borrower base across multiple operational entities in energy services sector
• Experienced administrative agent (PNC Bank) with syndicated lender group
• Comprehensive security package including equity pledges and insurance requirements
• Post-closing covenant structure provides additional operational oversight

**Principal Risks and Mitigating Factors:**
• Energy sector exposure with inherent commodity price volatility
• Complex multi-entity structure across different jurisdictions may complicate administration
• Recent merger activity introduces integration risks and operational complexity
• Post-closing deliverable requirements create potential compliance risks
• Multiple amendments to original agreement may indicate previous covenant or performance issues
